result.title: TRACER: Trace-Regularized Training Against Indirect Prompt Injection
result.comment: 19 pages, 13 figures, 12 tables. Accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026
result.summary: Indirect prompt injection uses untrusted retrieved content, tool outputs, or agent messages to override an LLM's intended behavior. We show that defense robustness is channel-conditioned: the same attack succeeds 18% of the time as a follow-up message but 53% when placed in retrieved context. We propose TRACER (Trace-Regularized Adversarial Channel Exposure with Reward-shaping), a channel-aware adversarial training method that samples presentation wrappers and combines an answer-anchored, evidence-gated reward with ATRC, which aligns attacked reasoning with clean evidence when an injection is invalid. On GSM8K with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, TRACER reduces RAG-framed ASR from 65.5% to 6.1% while preserving 78-82% clean accuracy. Joint RAG+tool training achieves 13.9% average ASR across framings at 3B scale, while a single epoch at 7B reaches 9.4%. These results demonstrate that robust defenses must explicitly train and evaluate across deployment channels.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究间接提示注入防御，发现攻击成功率依赖注入所处通道，提出通道感知对抗训练 TRACER：采样多种呈现包装，并用答案锚定、证据门控的奖励与 ATRC 将受攻击推理对齐到干净证据。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据门控奖励」与把受攻击推理轨迹对齐干净证据的监督设计，可能为 LVR 的推理轨迹训练、证据筛选与贡献分配提供可核查的线索，但属纯文本安全场景，具体联系尚需确认。
